verses.text: Joash became king in the seventh year that Jehu was king of Israel, and he ruled in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
Joash did what was right in the LORD's eyes all the years that Jehoiada the priest taught him.
But the high places were not removed. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense there.

Joash said to the priests, "Collect all the money brought as holy gifts to the LORD's temple: the money from the census, the money people pay for their vows, and the money people bring because they want to give it to the LORD's temple.
Let each priest receive the money from the people he serves. Then use it to repair any damage you find in the temple."
But by the twenty-third year that King Joash ruled, the priests still had not repaired the temple.

So King Joash called Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and asked them, "Why are you not repairing the damage to the temple? From now on, do not keep any more money from the people you serve. Hand it over for repairing the temple."
The priests agreed not to collect any more money from the people, and not to be in charge of repairing the temple themselves.

Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest and drilled a hole in its lid. He put it beside the altar, on the right side as people enter the LORD's temple. The priests who guarded the entrance put into the chest all the money that people brought to the LORD's temple.
Whenever they saw that there was a lot of money in the chest, the king's secretary and the high priest came. They counted the money that had been brought to the LORD's temple and put it into bags.
Then they gave the measured money to the men in charge of the work on the LORD's temple. These men paid the carpenters and builders who worked on the LORD's temple,
the stonemasons and stonecutters. They also used it to buy wood and cut stone for repairing the LORD's temple, and to pay for everything else needed to repair it.
The money brought to the LORD's temple was not used to make silver cups, wick trimmers, bowls, trumpets, or any other objects of gold or silver for the temple.
Instead, it was paid to the workers, who used it to repair the LORD's temple.
They did not ask the men in charge to account for the money given to them to pay the workers, because they were completely honest.
The money from the guilt offerings and the sin offerings was not brought into the LORD's temple. It belonged to the priests.
About that time Hazael king of Syria attacked Gath and captured it. Then he decided to attack Jerusalem.

So Joash king of Judah took all the holy things that his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, the kings of Judah, had given to God, as well as his own gifts. He took all the gold found in the treasuries of the LORD's temple and of the palace, and he sent it all to Hazael king of Syria. Then Hazael pulled back from Jerusalem.
The rest of what Joash did, and all his deeds, are written in the book of the history of the kings of Judah.
His officials made a plot against him and killed Joash at Beth Millo, on the road that goes down to Silla.
The officials who killed him were Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer. He died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. His son Amaziah became king after him.
